Fold

Hold one section closed by default, with a summary line that states its verdict and a grade chip, so the reader can skim every verdict and open only what they need.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1Group headerMono caps group name (Decide, Evidence, System, Method) and a one-line note on what the group holdstext, text-secondary
2FoldA native details on the surface, one hairline border; closed by defaultsurface, border
3Titleh2 in mono caps at the label step, inside the summarytext-secondary, --fs-label
4VerdictBody text: the fold's answer in one line, so a closed fold still says what it foundtext
5Grade chip28 Chip naming the grade or the count it rests on, in its one colour meaningplain, cyan, green, gold, red
6ChevronA drawn caret that turns a quarter on open; hidden in printtext-secondary, hover cyan
7BodyThe evidence: any kit organism or molecule, stacked with a 12px gapnone

Usage

Use it when

  • A section has a verdict a reader can act on without opening it.
  • A page has more than three sections and the reader comes to decide, not to read every word.

Do not use it when

  • Do not hide the next move in a fold: the first screen must carry it.
  • Do not write a summary that only names the section (Signal); it must state the verdict (He was about to build your tool).
  • Do not colour the chip for decoration. Colour has one meaning across the kit (arc weld spec 4.3): red a failed check, gold a limit, green proven, cyan an action or focus, plain (steel) unknown, magenta a paradox.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
groups[]{name, note, folds[]}noOptional grouping; the recoil-skim order is Decide, Evidence, System, Method.
folds[]{id, title, verdict, chip, tone, body}yesid is the anchor a skim row links to; tone is the chip colour by its one meaning.

Access

  • A native details and summary: Enter and Space open it, and screen readers announce expanded or collapsed.
  • A link to a fold's id opens it (the page script sets open on hash change).
  • The verdict is text, so the fold reads without colour; the chip names its grade in words.
  • Print opens every fold (the page script sets open before printing); the chevron is hidden in print.
